name: A thermocycler program
description: one named program as it is loaded on the lab's thermocyclers — its steps, their temperatures and durations, and what it is for; the thing a construction file or labsheet means when it says "run GG1"
phrases: the shape of a thermocycler program
what is the gibson thermocycler setting

name.description: the name as the machine carries it and a labsheet writes it, case-sensitive. The PrimeSTAR GXL family encodes its own parameters — PG<size>K<anneal>, so PG6K55 is a 6 kb target at 55 C with extension at 1 min/kb. The two Taq programs are named by annealing temperature alone: '45' and '55'.

steps.description: the program in order. NULL means the conditions are not recorded, which is NOT an empty program: `incomplete` must then be true.

temp_c.description: the block temperature for a hold

time_s.description: seconds. ZERO MEANS AN INFINITE HOLD — the terminal 16 C that runs until somebody opens the lid — and NULL means the duration is unrecorded. These are opposite findings and must never be collapsed: a scheduler that reads null as 0 promises a slot for a run whose length nobody knows.

steps.description: a cycle's inner steps, which are holds. NESTING STOPS HERE ON PURPOSE: no program the lab runs puts a cycle inside a cycle, and expressing arbitrary recursion would need `$ref`, which this installation's checker cannot verify — so the schema would be carried as validated while never being checked at all.

temp_c.description: the block temperature for a hold

time_s.description: seconds. ZERO MEANS AN INFINITE HOLD — the terminal 16 C that runs until somebody opens the lid — and NULL means the duration is unrecorded. These are opposite findings and must never be collapsed: a scheduler that reads null as 0 promises a slot for a run whose length nobody knows.

target_kb.description: the product size the program was built for. Advisory: the machine does not enforce it.

incomplete.description: TRUE WHEN THE LAB RUNS THIS PROGRAM AND NOBODY HAS WRITTEN DOWN WHAT IT DOES. Not a draft and not a deprecation — a program in active use whose definition is missing, which is more urgent than one that does not exist. GIB2 was this until 2026-10-15.

unknown.description: which parts are missing, named one by one. 'the duration of the 50 C hold' tells somebody what to measure; a bare `incomplete: true` does not.

source.description: where the conditions were transcribed from, so a reader can check them rather than trust them.

notes: WHY THIS SCHEMA EXISTS. On 2026-10-14 a student asked which thermocycler program to use for a Gibson, because the machine had no Gibson setting. The program GIB2 was named on three issued labpackets and its conditions were recorded nowhere — not in the labsheets, not in the tutorials, not in this repository. Meanwhile GG1 existed in three places at once, one of which `protocols/modules/golden_gate_assembly.js` already flagged as wrong. A program is an object the lab runs, and it needed one home and one shape. THE DEFINITION AVOIDS $ref/$defs/oneOf DELIBERATELY (2026-10-15): engine/c11/schema.py checks a closed keyword set and REFUSES a definition it cannot verify, rather than carrying it as validated. The first version used all three and `cortex health` caught it — the schema would have looked checked and never been checked. Cycle nesting is therefore written out one level, which is every program the lab actually runs.
